Notices.text: Part of my work is published and made available as part of the Urban Toolkit, an ecosystem of open-source tools, frameworks, knowledge bases, and methods designed to simplify and accelerate urban data visualization and analysis. For papers, guides, and code, check here.

Prospective students: I am always looking for self-motivated and hard-working PhD students interested in conducting and publishing research. While my work spans a broad range of computer science areas (e.g., machine learning, data management), my primary focus is on visualization and visual analytics. The easiest way to be considered is to apply directly to the PhD program (more info here) and, on your application, indicate your interest in working with me. Please note that I might not be able to offer feedback or guidance on admission or supervision before you apply to the program, but feel free to reach out. To help me respond as effectively as possible, please keep your messages (1) short and focused, (2) clearly tailored to my work, and (3) specific about fit (for example, referencing a particular paper or project of mine and briefly describing a research idea you’d like to pursue). Generic, broad, or non-specific emails are unlikely to receive a substantive reply.
